'''María Jesús (Iosune) Uriz Lespe''' (Estella, Navarra; 25 December 1949) is a pioneer in [[Taxonomy (biology)|taxonomy]], [[biology]] and [[population genetics]] of marine sponges, with a wide international recognition.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Worldcat Identities: Uriz Lespe, María Jesús|url=https://worldcat.org/identities/np-uriz%20lespe,%20maria%20jesus/|website=worldcat.org}}{{Dead link|date=September 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Iosune Uriz|url=https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=IBb0xwkAAAAJ&hl=en|access-date=2021-03-08|website=scholar.google.com}}</ref> In recent years{{When|date=May 2025}} she has focused her research on evolutionary and functional aspects of the symbiotic relationships between [[sponge]]s and [[microorganism]]s, interacting with the renowned American specialist [[Lynn Margulis]]. Her line of research in the biological activities of sponge [[secondary metabolites]] gave rise to a continued collaboration with pharmaceutical companies that have allowed the development of antitumor drugs.

==Biography==
She graduated at the [[University of Navarra]] in 1972. Later, in 1978, she received her doctorate Cum Laude in biology from the [[University of Barcelona]].<ref>{{Cite book|last=Jesús.|first=Uriz Lespe, María|title=Contribución a la fauna de esponjas (demospongia) de Catalunya|date=1987|publisher=Universitat Autonoma de Barcelona, Collegi Universitari de Girona|oclc=633903403}}</ref> Thanks to a postdoctoral fellowship from the Spanish Ministry of Education and Science, in 1973 she arrived at the [https://digital.csic.es/handle/10261/152009 Institute of Fisheries Research in Blane] s. Later, in 1985, she joined the [https://www.ceab.csic.es/en/ Center for Advanced Studies in Blanes] (CEAB-CSIC). She was vice-director at CEAB between 1985 and 1994, and director from 1994 to 1998.

She was one of the first researchers in Spain to use the autonomous diving suit. Her research has been developed mainly in the [[Mediterranean Sea|Mediterranean]] and [[Antarctica]] where she has described more than 30 new species.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Category:María Jesús Uriz Lespe taxa|url=https://species.wikimedia.org/wiki/Category:Mar%C3%ADa_Jes%C3%BAs_Uriz_Lespe_taxa|access-date=2021-03-08|website=species.wikimedia.org|language=en}}</ref> She is currently an emeritus research professor at the Center for Advanced Studies of Blanes (CEAB-CSIC),<ref>{{Cite web|title=Uriz Lespe, María Jesús|url=http://www.ceab.csic.es/personal/uriz-lespe-iosune/|access-date=2021-03-08|website=www.ceab.csic.es}}</ref> belonging to the [[Spanish National Research Council]].

==Research==
She has directed more than 15 doctoral theses and is the author of more than 150 articles published in indexed journals. She has directed more than 30 national and international projects. She is editor of the magazines [[Scientia Marina]] (2004–present) and [[Scientific Reports]] (2017–present). She is also an evaluator of scientific projects for the following organizations: CYCIT, [[CIRIT]], [[Banco Bilbao Vizcaya Argentaria|BBVA]], [[Smithsonian Institution|Smithsonian Institution of Washington]], [[National Science Foundation]] of the USA and of the [[European Union]]. She is Member of the Academic Commission of the Biodiversity Doctorate Program and the Marine Sciences Doctorate Program of the [[University of Barcelona]] and member of the Commission for the Evaluation of Collaborators and Lecturers of the University of Barcelona and Gerona (AQU).<ref>{{Cite web|title=Browsing by Author "Uriz Lespe, María Jesús"|url=http://m.diobma.udg.edu/browse?value=Uriz+Lespe,+Mar%C3%ADa+Jes%C3%BAs&type=author|access-date=2021-03-08|website=m.diobma.udg.edu}}</ref>

==Awards and honors==
In 2005, she obtained the "[[Narcís Monturiol]]" award for Scientific and Technical Merit<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=Medallas Narcís Monturiol|url=http://universitatsirecerca.gencat.cat/es/01_secretaria_duniversitats_i_recerca/premis_i_reconeixements/guardons_narcis_monturiol/medalles_narcis_monturiol/index.html|access-date=2021-03-08|website=Universidades e Investigación|language=es-ES}}</ref> for her scientific career, awarded by the [[Generalitat de Catalunya|Generalitat of Catalonia]].

==Highlighted publications==
* M Maldonado, MC Carmona, MJ Uriz, A Cruzado (1999). [[doi:10.1038/44560|Decline in Mesozoic reef-building sponges explained by silicon limitation]]. Nature 401 (6755), 785-788[1<nowiki>]</nowiki>
* MJ Uriz, X Turon, MA Becerro, G Agell (2003). [[DOI: 10.1002/jemt.10395|Siliceous spicules and skeleton frameworks in sponges: origin, diversity, ultrastructural patterns, and biological functions]]. Microscopy research and technique 62 (4), 279-299[2]
* MA Becerro, NI Lopez, X Turon, MJ Uriz (1994). [[doi:10.1016/0022-0981(94)90114-7|Antimicrobial activity and surface bacterial film in marine sponges]]. Journal of Experimental Marine Biology and Ecology 179 (2), 195-205[3]
* A Blanquer, MJ Uriz (2011). “[[DOI: 10.1093/molbev/msr096|Living together apart”: the hidden genetic diversity of sponge populations]]. Molecular biology and evolution 28 (9), 2435-2438
* E Cebrian, MJ Uriz, J Garrabou, E Ballesteros (2011). [[doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0020211|Sponge mass mortalities in a warming Mediterranean Sea: are cyanobacteria-harboring species worse off?]]. PLoS One 6 (6)[4]
* MJ Uriz (2006). [http://dx.doi.org/10.1139/Z06-032 Mineral skeletogenesis in sponges]. Canadian Journal of Zoology 84 (2), 322-356[5]
* MA Becerro, RW Thacker, X Turon, MJ Uriz, VJ Paul (2003). [[DOI: 10.1007/s00442-002-1138-7|Biogeography of sponge chemical ecology: comparisons of tropical and temperate defenses]].Oecologia 135 (1), 91-101[6]
* M Maldonado, MJ Uriz (1999). [[doi:10.1038/19007|Sexual propagation by sponge fragments]]. Nature 398 (6727), 476-476[7]
* M Turon, MJ Uriz, D Martin (2019). [[doi:10.1128/mSystems.00148-19|Multipartner Symbiosis across Biological Domains: Looking at the Eukaryotic Associations from a Microbial Perspective]] MSystems 4 (4), e00148-19
